text.p: Portuguese bonds firmed in thin, cautious trade as the market wavered between fear of further dollar losses and optimism following Spain's CPI figure for February.
Dealers said Portuguese February inflation, which is due from Friday, was unlikely to bring any nasty surprises.
Economists forecast a monthly rise of between 0.2 and 0.4 to give year-on-year inflation of 2.8 to 3.0 percent.
"The market is divided over whether we should focus on U.S. factors or look at our own fundamentals, including what is likely to be a benign inflation number," said one trader.
Dealers said lower Spanish inflation might give the Bank of Spain room to cut its repo rate on Friday.
"If Spain cuts its rate and our CPI is within the forecast range, the Bank of Portugal will cut its rate for injecting funds next week," said one trader.
The Bank of Portugal currently injects funds at 6.50 percent.
